target_customer: Architecture, engineering and construction firms and general contractors reviewing BIM models across office and field teams
problem: Construction teams struggle to review and coordinate large 3D building models, and issues found late are costly.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for BIM model review (VR and web viewer)
product_category: BIM viewer and VR model review for construction

founders.name: Angel Alonso Say
education: Columbia University, Mechanical Engineering and Computer Science
founders.background_notes: YC page says he previously worked on computer vision software for the semiconductor industry (employer not named). TechCrunch says he started the company after a winning hack at the 2014 TechCrunch Disrupt Hackathon.

founders.name: Russell Varriale
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him Say's college roommate and co-founder. No further background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Converting large BIM and architectural models to run in VR headsets in 2015 and 2016 required real-time 3D optimisation on immature hardware; later Quest support for very large Revit models was hard.

defensibility.rationale: Model loading engines are hard but Autodesk and Revizto could add VR viewing; the company's value rested on engineering and integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an acquisition; in 2025 Resolve and Revizto announced an integration, treating each other as complementary.

market_need_then: Construction lacked a simple way to walk through BIM models in VR; TechCrunch reported more than 4,000 projects hosted and about 2,500 models processed by August 2016 and said other startups focused on real estate walk-throughs rather than architecture and construction.

branding.domain_note: Uses resolvebim.com, a BIM suffix on the real word; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain positioning as GoToMeeting in virtual reality, per a MarketScale quote from Say

rebrands.why: Not stated; a press release in June 2020 launched Resolve as a product and listings say the company later took the Resolve name. A Craft profile lists vrban as an earlier name.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name with a rename after the original InsiteVR brand; limited evidence of brand awareness beyond trade press.

pivots.from: VR walk-through of architectural models for design review (InsiteVR)
pivots.to: Resolve, BIM review for construction on Oculus Quest and web with large model support
pivots.why: Standalone headsets and demand from construction teams; stated launch focus is large BIM files on Quest

outcome_analysis: The company, first InsiteVR, raised a $1.5M seed in August 2016 with PlanGrid founders among the backers and later moved from design walkthroughs to construction BIM review under the Resolve name. It is still active with about 9 staff on the YC page, so it appears to have stalled at small scale without a large later round found in sources.
notes: The company was InsiteVR at the time of the batch; the YC page now lists Resolve. Competitor list is empty because the one dated source (TechCrunch 2016-08) names none; Navisworks, Revizto and Fuzor appear only in undated or later pages. Aggregators give totals of $1.5M to $5.2M and one lists $500K convertible note in 2015; unverified and not recorded. Founding year varies across sources (2014, 2015, 2021). The YC page lists 9 team members while the shard says active.
